title: distro-agnostic-cni-transformer-and-offline-metadata-index
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: on-prem/private installs run across a wide variety of Kubernetes distro variants (kubeadm, k3s, rke2, bottlerocket variants) and customers in air-gapped environments need the installer to reliably apply a compatible CNI stack from a vendored bundle. This PR introduces a lightweight distro-agnostic CNI transformer and an offline metadata index that lets the installer pick and patch the correct CNI manifests at install time without pulling anything from the public internet.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds installer/pkg/transformer: a small binary that consumes vendored CNI manifest templates and applies distro-specific transform rules (serviceAccount, hostPort vs hostNetwork, crd ordering shims).
- Adds an offline metadata index (assets/offline-index.yaml) that lists vendored image digests, helm/manifest mapping, and per-distro transform rules (k3s, rke2, kubeadm). The index is generated by scripts/generate-offline-index.sh and consumed by the transformer.
- Extends the Helm chart (charts/installer) to accept pre-seeded CRDs and provide a cniMode override (managed | vendor | passthrough).
- Terraform module changes (terraform/modules/airgap): expose var.cni_mode and a preseed_assets S3/OCI var so customers can point to their seeded registry.
- Adds e2e test vectors for k3s and rke2 that run the transformer against vendored bundles (test/airgap/e2e-cni.sh).
- Improves checksumming and OCI mirror index generation to ensure deterministic offline artifacts (scripts/offline-index-checksum).

Files of interest (summary):
- installer/pkg/transformer/transformer.go (core transformer logic)
- assets/offline-index.yaml (generated index sample)
- scripts/generate-offline-index.sh (index generator)
- charts/installer/values.yaml (new cniMode controls)
- terraform/modules/airgap/main.tf (expose cni vars)
- docs/offline-cni.md (design + upgrade notes)

Checklist: 
- [x] Transformer binary + unit tests
- [x] Offline index generation script + sample index
- [x] Helm chart cniMode and CRD preseed support
- [x] Terraform variable surfaces and example usage
- [x] Minimal docs and upgrade notes
- [x] E2E smoke test for k3s/rke2 paths

Why this approach: shipping a small transform step keeps the vendored bundles smaller (no multiple distro-specific copies) while giving a deterministic, auditable way to adapt manifests to cluster distro constraints at install time. The index file is intentionally compact (image digests + transform rule refs) to make offline seeding and verification straightforward.

Backward compatibility and upgrade path: default behavior remains cniMode=managed (current behavior). When a customer opts into cniMode=vendor, the installer will read the offline index and run the transformer. Documents in docs/offline-cni.md describe how to upgrade a cluster to use vendor mode and provide a rollback procedure (installer rollback hook will revert transformed manifests and resume managed CNI).

ci_log_summary: Initial CI: lint fail -> fixed. Second run: unit + build passed. Integration smoke initially flaky on registry seed; fixed by retry logic. Final run: all checks passed (build, unit, integration-smoke, helm-lint, terraform-validate).
release_notes: Adds an offline CNI transformer and a compact offline metadata index for air-gapped installs. Exposes cniMode in Helm and Terraform to select vendor-managed CNI artifacts. Improves deterministic checksums for offline bundles. Backwards compatible by default (managed mode).
notes_for_ops: When seeding offline registries, ensure assets/offline-index.yaml is placed alongside vendor images and the installer is invoked with --preseed-registry pointing to the mirror. The transformer is safe to run multiple times (idempotent) but the upgrade path recommends a canary rollout on a single cluster before mass enabling vendor mode.
testing_instructions: make offline-index && ./scripts/generate-offline-index.sh --source ./vendored && helm template charts/installer --values charts/installer/values.yaml --set cniMode=vendor | kubectl apply -f - --dry-run=client then run test/airgap/e2e-cni.sh against a local k3s or rke2 cluster to validate CRD ordering and image pull secrets.
